attribution.note: Marcus wrote this sentence himself in his own Substack post. It is not a quote of anyone else.

semantics.note: The wording follows his sentence exactly, and 'just the start' is firm forward-looking language. But it never says what follows: more stock losses, or the wider fallout that the hedged sentences around it describe.

contract.note: The contract is right that any test, such as a further price drop over some window or a broader crisis, would be one the evaluator chose, not Marcus. With no definite outcome stated, declining to set support or contradiction conditions is fair.

evidence.note: Kiplinger, 2026-11-12, before the cutoff. Huang resigned; the stock fell nearly 14% intraday and closed down 4.3%. This is relevant market context but cannot settle an outcome Marcus never specified.

reviews.rationale: 'That's just the start' is firm, but it names no outcome, size, metric or deadline. The next-day record (a 14% intraday plunge that recovered to a 4.3% loss) could count for or against it depending on a reading Marcus never gave. The claim is too vague to score, so it is not adjudicable rather than unresolved or broken.
